summary: Six experiments completed in 1.8 minutes, and five were compute-bound. The 1.64-minute Three-model live factor proposal authenticity preflight was the longest listed task, but the reconstructed timing does not show why it took longest.
bottlenecks_identified: Disk-mtime reconstruction ranks the tasks but provides no phase-level cause for the 1.64-minute compute leader.
The GPU snapshot is not linked to experiment boundaries or processes, so it cannot grade utilization across the compute-bound tasks; the locked classification reports no compute-bound GPU-idle fault.
No loaded-model concurrency or runner-selection record is available, so the data cannot determine whether any task with at least two models loaded in parallel missed DualGPURunner.
improvements_suggested: Emit monotonic start and stop times for model load, inference, validation, and artifact-write phases from the conductor.
Sample GPU utilization with experiment and process identifiers while each compute-bound task is active.
Record loaded-model count and selected runner for every compute task, and select DualGPURunner only when at least two models are loaded in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Replace disk-mtime reconstruction with a live per-phase execution ledger.
Join GPU samples to active experiment and process identifiers.
Add loaded-model-count and runner-selection fields to each compute-task receipt.
meta_reflection: The data can rank elapsed time but cannot attribute the runtime or quantify a faster path. The next retrospective needs task-linked phase, device, model-count, and dispatcher evidence.
